mechanism_narrative: A sustained three-week recovery in RETAIL_REC itself, from -30.4 to -24.1, reflects an ongoing reopening momentum that should continue mechanically into the next four weeks absent a shock, producing a further increase in mean RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each week from -30.4 to -24.1 over the snapshot
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days despite the prior three-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Rising TRANSIT mobility (from -24.4 to -19.0) indicates increasing out-of-home trip-taking capacity, which feeds directly into retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks as commuters resume discretionary stops.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -24.4 to -19.0 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks even though TRANSIT continues its upward trajectory.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL of more than 1 point, triggered once RESIDENTIAL drops below 8.5, signals households are spending measurably less time at home, which should coincide with higher RETAIL_REC in the following week as pent-up errands and leisure trips are executed.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.7 to 8.6 across the four weeks, crossing near 8.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week immediately following a RESIDENTIAL drop below 8.5.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT create a compounding effect on RETAIL_REC because commuting trips and workplace attendance jointly enable incidental retail stops before/after work, producing a stronger RETAIL_REC rise than either series would alone.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose each week while WORKPLACES fluctuated but remains above t-3w level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over 4 weeks is no greater than growth predicted from TRANSIT alone, indicating no interaction effect with WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility reverses and falls more than 4 points week-on-week (as seen from t-1w -24.4 to t-0w -28.6), this signals a re-tightening of policy restrictions that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks as workplace-linked trip chains collapse.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -24.4 at t-1w to -28.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise or holds steady over the next 2 weeks despite the WORKPLACES decline exceeding the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from 0.0 to 8.6) reflects growing comfort with routine out-of-home errands, which behaviorally generalizes to other discretionary categories like retail and recreation within the following four weeks as risk perception continues to ease.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose steadily from 0.0 to 8.6 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM continues rising, indicating no behavioral spillover.

mechanism_narrative: The partial recovery in PARKS mobility (from -39.4 to -33.1) combined with improving TRANSIT indicates increased outdoor and recreational travel appetite; when both series improve together by more than 5 points cumulatively over the snapshot, RETAIL_REC should rise in tandem over the next four weeks because recreation-adjacent retail (cafes, shops near parks) benefits from the same mobility recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both improve by more than 5 points cumulatively over the snapshot window
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -39.4 to -33.1 and TRANSIT improved from -24.4 to -19.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 4 weeks despite both PARKS and TRANSIT improving beyond the 5-point joint threshold.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state regime where RESIDENTIAL mobility has plateaued near 8.5-9.5 for multiple weeks without sharp movement, RETAIL_REC becomes driven primarily by seasonal/calendar effects rather than structural mobility shifts, and should mean-revert toward its recent four-week average rather than continue its prior trend.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays within a 1.5-point band for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 8.3 and 9.7 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues its strong upward trend over the next week rather than reverting toward the recent mean, despite RESIDENTIAL remaining in a tight stable band.
